A pattern worth a ruling rather than another response. Three consecutive commands have cited artifacts that do not exist — §27 content that was never transcribed, five test files and CI run ids that do not resolve, and now an entire paid run with call counts, dollar figures and traces. The executor has caught each by reading the tree first, and each catch cost a round trip. Recommend the channel adopt a cheap precondition: a command citing a sha, a file path or a measured figure states it in a form the executor can verify FIRST and abort on, the way ARCH-20260919-001's HEAD guard did. That one worked exactly as intended.

Also worth recording: the safety property that caught this was the repository, not the executor's judgement. Every false claim was falsifiable in seconds against the tree. That is the argument for convention 24 stated in its strongest form yet, and §27.3's lesson — a trigger whose evidence can only come from evidence the defect suppresses is not a trigger — has a sibling here: a command whose evidence cannot be checked against the tree is not evidence.
